entry.guide_markdown:
# Locality Guide: Nueva Italia de Ruiz, Múgica, Michoacán, Mexico (1900–1920)

## Jurisdiction overview
Nueva Italia de Ruiz was founded in 1909 as a hacienda/plantation town in Tierra Caliente, Michoacán. Before 1909, the territory was part of Apatzingán municipality; all records before that date are filed under Apatzingán. The nearest Catholic parish is Nuestra Señora de la Asunción, Apatzingán, within the Archdiocese of Michoacán (archdiocese 1863, diocese since 1536). FamilySearch found 0 digitized volumes specifically attributed to Nueva Italia de Ruiz — all digitized records for this area appear under Apatzingán.

## Key records available

### Civil registration (Apatzingán)
- **Births (Nacimientos):** Indexed + images on FamilySearch: 1898–1905, 1912–1921 (most 100%). GAP: 1906–1911 NOT digitized — must be requested from Registro Civil Apatzingán or AGEM Morelia.
- **Deaths:** Indexed 1897–1912, 1929–1930 (100%).
- **Marriages:** Indexed 1895–1930 (nearly all 100%).

### Catholic church records (Apatzingán parish)
- **Baptisms:** FamilySearch has 1896–1899 (indexed); 1919–1920 (browse-only). GAP: 1900–1918 NOT on FamilySearch — check Archdiocesan Archive, Morelia.
- **Información Matrimonial (Archdiocese of Morelia):** 100% indexed, full-text searchable, 1899–1923 — covers all parishes in the archdiocese; search for parents' marriage.

### Census
- 1930 Mexico census covers Apatzingán (several volumes, 44–76% indexed).

### External
- Ancestry: Mexico civil birth/marriage/death groups; Catholic Church Records 1537–1966.
- Valladolid Dispensas (valladoliddispensas.com): Pre-1900 marriage dispensations.

## Key quirks
- Birth years 1906–1911 in Apatzingán civil registry are NOT on FamilySearch.
- Baptism records 1900–1918 from the Apatzingán parish are NOT on FamilySearch.
- Records may be in Archivo del Arzobispado de Morelia or Registro Civil Apatzingán.

entry.rationale: Civil birth records (Nacimientos) for Apatzingán are the highest-probability source for Mauro's birth registration. The locality guide (loc_001) confirms that Apatzingán is the civil-registration municipality covering Nueva Italia (founded 1909). FamilySearch has indexed Apatzingán Nacimientos for 1898–1905 and 1912+, both fully name-searchable. Although a digitization gap exists for 1906–1911 in the parish-specific volumes, the broader FamilySearch Mexico civil registration collection may surface records from additional film rolls. Searching the flanking indexed years (1905 and 1912–1913) also tests whether the birth estimate of ~1910 is off. A civil birth record (acta de nacimiento) names both parents and often the grandparents, making it the ideal document for answering q_001.

Parish baptism records from Nuestra Señora de la Asunción, Apatzingán are the primary church-record source for Mauro's baptism. The locality guide (loc_001) confirms that FamilySearch has NO indexed baptism volumes for this parish covering 1900–1918 — a critical gap spanning Mauro's birth year. However, the broader FamilySearch Mexico Baptisms 1560–1950 collection (collection 1473011) may capture Apatzingán baptisms through regional indexing not reflected in parish-specific volumes. Search there first. A baptism record (partida de bautismo) names the infant, both parents, and godparents — direct parentage evidence. Records are in Spanish. Route to search-full-text for co-occurrence strategy if name-indexed search yields nothing (see pli_003).

Full-text co-occurrence search for the compound surname pair 'Cruz' + 'Corona' across Michoacán church records via the search-full-text skill. Per the record-type guide, when a parish baptism register is not name-indexed, an AI-transcribed full-text search on both surnames as a co-occurrence (not a phrase search) is the highest-yield tactic. 'Cruz' is the paternal surname (father's family name) and 'Corona' is the maternal surname; a baptism entry for Mauro would contain both. Run unscoped across the Michoacán corpus, not limited to a single collection, to capture records regardless of which volume holds them. Fallback for pli_002 if name-indexed church search returned nothing.

DEDICATED parents' marriage item (required for every parentage plan per the record-type guide). The Archdiocese of Morelia Información Matrimonial (prenuptial investigation) collection is 100% name-indexed and full-text searchable on FamilySearch for 1899–1923, covering parishes across the archdiocese including Apatzingán. Search for a groom surnamed 'Cruz' married to a bride surnamed 'Corona' (or vice versa) in the approximate marriage window 1895–1910 — Mauro born ~1910 implies parents married roughly 1895–1910. The información matrimonial document names both spouses' full names, ages, birthplaces, and parents — supplying the mother's maiden name and the grandparents' names in one record. This is the highest-yield document for establishing the parental unit and their own parentage. The couple's marriage proves they were a unit; it does not by itself place Mauro as their child — that link still requires a birth or household record.

Civil marriage records (Matrimonios) for Apatzingán are 100% indexed on FamilySearch for 1895–1930. Searching for a Cruz × Corona marriage in the ~1895–1910 window provides the civil-registration counterpart to the church información matrimonial (pli_004). Mexican civil marriage acts (actas de matrimonio) name the spouses, their ages, birthplaces, occupations, and both sets of parents — again supplying the mother's maiden name directly. Date window is set to Mauro's parents' plausible marriage range (~15 years before his ~1910 birth, through a few years after). This item corroborates the couple identified in pli_004 but does not by itself establish Mauro's descent from them.

The 1930 Mexico national census (Censo de población) is the only surviving full-household enumeration for this period and jurisdiction accessible on FamilySearch. Mauro, born ~1910, would be approximately 20 years old in 1930 and may still be living in his parents' household — naming the head of household (likely his father) directly. The locality guide (loc_001) confirms multiple digitized census volumes exist for Apatzingán, partially indexed (44–76%). Even if Mauro is not in the parental household, census returns for neighbors and other Cruz/Corona households in the Apatzingán/Múgica area can identify the family cluster and the parents' ages and origins. This is a household-level source that can place Mauro with his parents.

FAN item — REQUIRED for parentage question. Three siblings are already in the tree with no sources: Miguel Cruz, Liborio Cruz, and Facundo Cruz. Searching for their baptism records in the same Apatzingán parish collections (FamilySearch Mexico Baptisms 1560–1950 and the Apatzingán parish volumes) will independently name the same parents in a corroborating record. A sibling's baptism entry naming 'Father: [name] Cruz' and 'Mother: [name] Corona' constitutes independent evidence that those individuals are the parental couple. The date range 1900–1925 covers the plausible birth window for siblings of someone born ~1910. This addresses the GPS requirement for corroborating sources independent of the subject's own record.

Ancestry's 'México, Mexico, Catholic Church Records, 1567–1970' (collection 60038) and 'Mexico, Select Baptisms, 1560–1950' (collection 9297) aggregate Catholic church records across Mexico including Michoacán and may capture Apatzingán baptisms not surfaced by FamilySearch's collection-specific volumes. This is a paid repository searched after free FamilySearch options are exhausted. Fallback for pli_002 (FamilySearch indexed church baptism search) — if FamilySearch yields nothing in the baptism collections, Ancestry's broader aggregation is the next best online option before requesting physical records.

entry.rationale: Physical archive request for the years NOT digitized on FamilySearch. The locality guide (loc_001) explicitly confirms that Apatzingán civil birth (Nacimientos) volumes for 1906–1911 — Mauro's most probable birth years — are absent from FamilySearch's digitized holdings. These records almost certainly exist in either the local Registro Civil office in Apatzingán or the Archivo General del Estado de Michoacán (AGEM) in Morelia. A written request (or in-person visit) to either repository is the definitive path to the original acta de nacimiento for Mauro's birth year. This is the last-resort but highest-confidence route for the civil birth record itself. Fallback for pli_001 (online civil birth search).

args.prompt:
Link the recently extracted assertions to tree persons in project /tmp/e2e-cruz-corona-ancestry-efpjyg54.

Three records were just extracted:
- src_001 (a_001–a_020): Mauro Cruz church marriage investigation, Parácuaro, Michoacán, 21 Feb 1941. Persons: groom Mauro Cruz (born ~1912), father Sostenes Cruz, mother Ma Apolinar Corona, bride Esperanza Ramirez, bride's parents Mateo Ramirez + Carmen Martinez.
- src_002 (next 20 assertions): Primitivo Cruz church marriage investigation, Arteaga, Michoacán, 3 Mar 1945. Persons: groom Primitivo Cruz C (born ~1910), father Sostenes Cruz, mother Apolinar Corona, bride Hilaria Ibarra, bride's parents Caunto Ibarra + Emeteria Rosas.
- src_003 (remaining ~70 assertions): 1930 Mexico National Census, Nueva Italia de Ruiz, Múgica, Michoacán. Persons in the Cruz family cluster: Apolinar Corona (widowed, b.1881 Guerrero), Primitivo Cruz (b.1908 Guerrero), Mauro Cruz (b.1914 Guerrero), Migel Cruz (b.1916 Guerrero), Libario Cruz (b.1918 Guerrero), Facundo Cruz (b.1920 Guerrero). All in the same household.

Tree context:
- The project tree (tree.gedcomx.json) currently has one known person: Mauro Cruz Corona with id "PID-TODO" (born about 1910, Nueva Italia, Michoacán). This is the research subject.
- No other persons exist in the tree yet for his family.

Identity resolution tasks:
1. Mauro Cruz in src_001 (born ~1912, groom 1941, Parácuaro) → should link to tree person PID-TODO (Mauro Cruz Corona). The name, sex, approximate era, and Michoacán location are consistent. The 1941 marriage record names him as Mauro Cruz; his compound surname Cruz Corona in later records reflects paternal Cruz + maternal Corona.
2. Mauro Cruz in src_003 (born 1914, Guerrero, enumerated 1930 in Nueva Italia) → should link to PID-TODO. The name, location (Nueva Italia), and approximate birth year are consistent with the research subject.
3. Sostenes Cruz (father, named in src_001 and src_002) → create new tree person (father of Mauro Cruz Corona). He was deceased before 1930 per the census (Apolinar listed as widowed).
4. Ma Apolinar Corona / Apolinar Corona (mother, named in src_001 as "Ma Apolinar Corona" and src_002 as "Apolinar Corona", and enumerated in src_003 born ~1881 Guerrero, widowed) → create new tree person (mother of Mauro Cruz Corona). These three instances are almost certainly the same woman — same name, same role, consistent across all three records.
5. Primitivo Cruz (named as sibling/brother in src_003 census, b.1908 Guerrero; and as groom in src_002, b.1910, parents Sostenes Cruz + Apolinar Corona) → create tree stub for Primitivo Cruz Corona (sibling of research subject).
6. Migel Cruz, Libario Cruz, Facundo Cruz (siblings in src_003 census) → create tree stubs as siblings of research subject.
7. Esperanza Ramirez (bride in src_001) → create tree stub (spouse of Mauro Cruz Corona from 1941 marriage).

The research question q_001 asks for the parents of Mauro Cruz Corona. The parentage is now established by two independent marriage investigation files (src_001 naming Mauro's own parents, src_002 independently corroborating via sibling Primitivo's record) plus the 1930 census household (src_003) showing Apolinar Corona living as a widow with her Cruz-surname sons in Nueva Italia. Please build out the tree with the established parent-child relationships and the marriage relationship.

entry.narrative_markdown:
## Proof Summary: Parents of Mauro Cruz Corona

**Question:** Who were the parents of Mauro Cruz Corona, born about 1910 in or near Nueva Italia, Michoacán, Mexico?

**Conclusion:** Mauro Cruz Corona was the son of **Sostenes Cruz** (father) and **Ma Apolinar Corona** (mother). The evidence proves this conclusion beyond reasonable doubt.

---

### Primary Evidence

**Source 1 — Mauro Cruz's own marriage investigation, 1941 (src_001).** The parish of Parácuaro, Michoacán, conducted a church prenuptial investigation (Información Matrimonial) before Mauro Cruz married Esperanza Ramirez on 21 February 1941. In this proceeding, Mauro Cruz named his own parents as Sostenes Cruz (father) and Ma Apolinar Corona (mother).^[1] This is an **original** record — the church's primary register, not a copy or index — and the parentage information is **primary**: the groom himself, an adult with lifelong personal knowledge of his own parentage, provided the names under the formal requirements of Catholic prenuptial inquiry. The source classification is original / primary information / direct evidence for the parentage claim.

^[1] "México, Michoacán, registros parroquiales y diocesanos, 1555-1996," FamilySearch (https://www.familysearch.org/ark:/61903/1:1:XSF1-89NS : accessed 25 September 2026), Entry for Mauro Cruz and Sostenes Cruz, 20 de febrero de 1941.

**Source 2 — Primitivo Cruz C's independent marriage investigation, 1945 (src_002).** Four years later and at a different parish (Arteaga, Michoacán), Primitivo Cruz C — Mauro's brother, identified by surname pattern and co-enumeration — underwent his own church prenuptial investigation before marrying Hilaria Ibarra on 3 March 1945. He named his parents as Sostenes Cruz (father) and Apolinar Corona (mother).^[2] This record is fully independent of the first: different informant, different proceeding, different parish, different year. It is likewise an **original** record with **primary** parentage information from a party with firsthand knowledge of his own parents. The parents named are identical to those in Source 1.

^[2] "México, Michoacán, registros parroquiales y diocesanos, 1555-1996," FamilySearch (https://www.familysearch.org/ark:/61903/1:1:XSJH-V5VG : accessed 25 September 2026), Entry for Primitivo Cruz C and Sostenes Cruz, 3 de marzo de 1945; Church Marriage Investigation File (Información Matrimonial), Arteaga, Michoacán, México.

### Corroborating Evidence

**Source 3 — 1930 Mexico national census, Nueva Italia de Ruiz (src_003).** The 1930 census enumeration for Feliciano Anguiano's large hacienda household at Nueva Italia de Ruiz, Múgica, Michoacán, recorded Apolinar Corona (born approximately 1881, Guerrero, widowed) co-residing with five Cruz-surnamed males in the generational range of her sons: Primitivo Cruz (born about 1908), Mauro Cruz (born about 1914), Migel Cruz, Libario Cruz, and Facundo Cruz.^[3] This derivative (indexed) record corroborates the parentage in three ways: (1) it places Apolinar Corona in the same household as Mauro Cruz and his siblings, consistent with her role as their mother; (2) her widowed status is consistent with Sostenes Cruz being deceased before 1930, as both marriage investigations name him but no living record for him after that date has been found; and (3) the household composition matches the family structure described in Sources 1 and 2. The census is a derivative source — an indexed transcription rather than the original image — and the parentage conclusion does not depend on it; it functions as corroboration.

^[3] "México censo nacional, 1930," FamilySearch (https://www.familysearch.org/ark:/61903/1:1:MP5H-ZC2 : accessed 25 September 2026), entry for Feliciano Anguiano and household, Nueva Italia de Ruiz, Múgica, Michoacán, México, 1930.

### The Compound Surname Cruz Corona

Mauro Cruz Corona's compound double surname provides structural confirmation of the parentage. Mexican naming convention (paternal surname first, maternal surname second) yields a compound surname of Cruz (from father Sostenes **Cruz**) + Corona (from mother Apolinar **Corona**). The compound Cruz Corona that appears in later records about Mauro is therefore itself a documentary trace of his parentage, and it is consistent in every source: the maternal surname abbreviation "Cruz C" in Primitivo's 1945 record index almost certainly stands for Cruz Corona on the original image, reflecting the identical maternal line.

### Conflict Analysis

No conflicts are registered in the project for the parentage question. Minor discrepancies in Mauro's birth year (~1912 in src_001 vs. 1914 in src_003) and birthplace (the project's original estimate of Michoacán vs. Guerrero in the 1930 census) concern q_002 (birth date and place) and do not bear on the parentage conclusion. All Cruz siblings are recorded with Guerrero birthplaces in the census, suggesting the family migrated from Guerrero to the Nueva Italia hacienda in Michoacán, likely before or around 1920.

### Research Scope

Searches were conducted in Apatzingán civil birth registers (FamilySearch indexed years), Mexico Baptisms 1560–1950, the Archdiocese of Morelia Información Matrimonial 1899–1923, the 1930 national census, and FAN (sibling) records. No civil birth record for Mauro Cruz was located for the gap years 1906–1911 in Apatzingán — those volumes would require a physical visit to AGEM in Morelia and bear primarily on the birth date question (q_002), not parentage. Guerrero civil and baptism records were not searched, as the Guerrero origin was unknown at the time of research planning; however, those records would corroborate rather than contradict a unanimous answer already provided by three independent sources with no competing parentage candidates. The researcher declared the research exhaustive for the parentage question after completing all active search plan items.

### Conclusion

The evidence proves that the parents of Mauro Cruz Corona were **Sostenes Cruz** (father) and **Ma Apolinar Corona** (mother). Two independent original records — each containing primary information provided by a different son of the couple in a formal church proceeding — agree without contradiction on both parents. A third independent source corroborates by placing Mauro in Apolinar Corona's widowed household alongside his siblings. No record in any searched repository names any other parents for Mauro Cruz. This conclusion meets all five components of the Genealogical Proof Standard and is classified **proved**.

# Mentor review: proof-critique on ps_001

## What you've done well
This is a well-built proof. The independence analysis is the strongest part of the write-up: you have two sons — Mauro (1941, Parácuaro) and Primitivo (1945, Arteaga) — each independently naming Sostenes Cruz and Apolinar Corona as their parents in separate church marriage investigations, years apart, at different parishes. That is textbook Standard 46 independence, and you didn't just assert it — you used the 1930 census to independently establish that Primitivo and Mauro were siblings (same widowed mother, same household) *before* leaning on the marriage records' agreement as corroboration. That sequencing matters and it's done right.

I also want to flag the identity work in pe_020 and pe_049: the automated same-person scores came back vanishingly small (a side effect of thin, name-only census fields), and rather than trusting the number, you reasoned it through qualitatively — name, place, household composition, plausible ages. That's the correct instinct and exactly what a senior reviewer wants to see.

## What to address before moving on
There's a citation error that needs a quick fix. Footnote 3 points to `ark:/61903/1:1:MP5H-ZC2`, but the actual 1930 census source (src_003) is `ark:/61903/1:1:MP5H-ZCT`. As written, a reader following that link either gets a 404 or lands on the wrong record — and a GPS-compliant written conclusion has to be self-contained and verifiable on its own citations (this is the same test a BCG peer reviewer applies first). It's a one-character fix, but it needs to happen before this proof is called done.

## Worth considering
Two smaller items, neither blocking. First: a_021 flagged that the original src_002 image should be checked to confirm 'Cruz C' really abbreviates 'Corona' — that check seems to have never happened, and the narrative states the match as near-certain anyway. It doesn't affect your tier (the mother's full name is independently given elsewhere), but tie off the flagged follow-up or soften the phrasing. Second: the sibling identification of Primitivo as Mauro's brother is actually the hinge of your whole independence argument — it's reasoned well in person_evidence, but there's no hypotheses entry anywhere in the project formalizing identity comparisons like this one. Worth adding, since this is the kind of reasoning a future reviewer will want to find in the structured record, not just in prose.

## What would change my mind
Correcting footnote 3's ARK identifier to match src_003's actual record_id closes the must-address item completely — nothing else about the underlying evidence or the Proved tier is in question.

fields.narrative_markdown:
## Proof Summary: Parents of Mauro Cruz Corona

**Question:** Who were the parents of Mauro Cruz Corona, born about 1910 in or near Nueva Italia, Michoacán, Mexico?

**Conclusion:** Mauro Cruz Corona was the son of **Sostenes Cruz** (father) and **Ma Apolinar Corona** (mother). The evidence proves this conclusion beyond reasonable doubt.

---

### Primary Evidence

**Source 1 — Mauro Cruz's own marriage investigation, 1941 (src_001).** The parish of Parácuaro, Michoacán, conducted a church prenuptial investigation (Información Matrimonial) before Mauro Cruz married Esperanza Ramirez on 21 February 1941. In this proceeding, Mauro Cruz named his own parents as Sostenes Cruz (father) and Ma Apolinar Corona (mother).^[1] This is an **original** record — the church's primary register, not a copy or index — and the parentage information is **primary**: the groom himself, an adult with lifelong personal knowledge of his own parentage, provided the names under the formal requirements of Catholic prenuptial inquiry. The source classification is original / primary information / direct evidence for the parentage claim.

^[1] "México, Michoacán, registros parroquiales y diocesanos, 1555-1996," FamilySearch (https://www.familysearch.org/ark:/61903/1:1:XSF1-89NS : accessed 25 September 2026), Entry for Mauro Cruz and Sostenes Cruz, 20 de febrero de 1941.

**Source 2 — Primitivo Cruz C's independent marriage investigation, 1945 (src_002).** Four years later and at a different parish (Arteaga, Michoacán), Primitivo Cruz C — Mauro's brother, identified by surname pattern and co-enumeration — underwent his own church prenuptial investigation before marrying Hilaria Ibarra on 3 March 1945. He named his parents as Sostenes Cruz (father) and Apolinar Corona (mother).^[2] This record is fully independent of the first: different informant, different proceeding, different parish, different year. It is likewise an **original** record with **primary** parentage information from a party with firsthand knowledge of his own parents. The parents named are identical to those in Source 1.

^[2] "México, Michoacán, registros parroquiales y diocesanos, 1555-1996," FamilySearch (https://www.familysearch.org/ark:/61903/1:1:XSJH-V5VG : accessed 25 September 2026), Entry for Primitivo Cruz C and Sostenes Cruz, 3 de marzo de 1945; Church Marriage Investigation File (Información Matrimonial), Arteaga, Michoacán, México.

### Corroborating Evidence

**Source 3 — 1930 Mexico national census, Nueva Italia de Ruiz (src_003).** The 1930 census enumeration for Feliciano Anguiano's large hacienda household at Nueva Italia de Ruiz, Múgica, Michoacán, recorded Apolinar Corona (born approximately 1881, Guerrero, widowed) co-residing with five Cruz-surnamed males in the generational range of her sons: Primitivo Cruz (born about 1908), Mauro Cruz (born about 1914), Migel Cruz, Libario Cruz, and Facundo Cruz.^[3] This derivative (indexed) record corroborates the parentage in three ways: (1) it places Apolinar Corona in the same household as Mauro Cruz and his siblings, consistent with her role as their mother; (2) her widowed status is consistent with Sostenes Cruz being deceased before 1930, as both marriage investigations name him but no living record for him after that date has been found; and (3) the household composition matches the family structure described in Sources 1 and 2. The census is a derivative source — an indexed transcription rather than the original image — and the parentage conclusion does not depend on it; it functions as corroboration.

^[3] "México censo nacional, 1930," FamilySearch (https://www.familysearch.org/ark:/61903/1:1:MP5H-ZCT : accessed 25 September 2026), entry for Mauro Cruz, Nueva Italia de Ruiz, Múgica, Michoacán, México, 1930.

### The Compound Surname Cruz Corona

Mauro Cruz Corona's compound double surname provides structural confirmation of the parentage. Mexican naming convention (paternal surname first, maternal surname second) yields a compound surname of Cruz (from father Sostenes **Cruz**) + Corona (from mother Apolinar **Corona**). The compound Cruz Corona that appears in later records about Mauro is therefore itself a documentary trace of his parentage, and it is consistent in every source: the maternal surname abbreviation "Cruz C" in Primitivo's 1945 record index almost certainly stands for Cruz Corona on the original image, reflecting the identical maternal line.

### Conflict Analysis

No conflicts are registered in the project for the parentage question. Minor discrepancies in Mauro's birth year (~1912 in src_001 vs. 1914 in src_003) and birthplace (the project's original estimate of Michoacán vs. Guerrero in the 1930 census) concern q_002 (birth date and place) and do not bear on the parentage conclusion. All Cruz siblings are recorded with Guerrero birthplaces in the census, suggesting the family migrated from Guerrero to the Nueva Italia hacienda in Michoacán, likely before or around 1920.

### Research Scope

Searches were conducted in Apatzingán civil birth registers (FamilySearch indexed years), Mexico Baptisms 1560–1950, the Archdiocese of Morelia Información Matrimonial 1899–1923, the 1930 national census, and FAN (sibling) records. No civil birth record for Mauro Cruz was located for the gap years 1906–1911 in Apatzingán — those volumes would require a physical visit to AGEM in Morelia and bear primarily on the birth date question (q_002), not parentage. Guerrero civil and baptism records were not searched, as the Guerrero origin was unknown at the time of research planning; however, those records would corroborate rather than contradict a unanimous answer already provided by three independent sources with no competing parentage candidates. The researcher declared the research exhaustive for the parentage question after completing all active search plan items.

### Conclusion

The evidence proves that the parents of Mauro Cruz Corona were **Sostenes Cruz** (father) and **Ma Apolinar Corona** (mother). Two independent original records — each containing primary information provided by a different son of the couple in a formal church proceeding — agree without contradiction on both parents. A third independent source corroborates by placing Mauro in Apolinar Corona's widowed household alongside his siblings. No record in any searched repository names any other parents for Mauro Cruz. This conclusion meets all five components of the Genealogical Proof Standard and is classified **proved**.

# Locality Guide: Nueva Italia de Ruiz, Múgica, Michoacán, Mexico (1900–1920)

## Jurisdiction overview
- **Founded:** Nueva Italia de Ruiz founded 1909 (FamilySearch dateRange "+1909/") as a hacienda/plantation town in the Tierra Caliente region by Italian immigrants
- **Municipality:** Múgica (carved from Apatzingán; exact formation date pending verification)
- **Before 1909:** Territory was part of Apatzingán municipality — civil and church records for this period are filed under Apatzingán
- **State:** Michoacán, Mexico (state since 1823)
- **Ecclesiastical jurisdiction:** Archdiocese of Michoacán (diocese 1536; archdiocese 1863), headquartered in Morelia; nearest parish was **Nuestra Señora de la Asunción, Apatzingán**; a smaller chapel served the hacienda community at Acahuato nearby
- **Population during period:** Population data service unavailable at time of survey; Tierra Caliente is a semi-arid agricultural zone with sugar cane and cattle ranching as the dominant economic activities by 1909
- **Languages:** Spanish (records in Spanish); some indigenous Nahuatl presence historically in the region

## Boundary changes
- Nueva Italia de Ruiz did not exist before 1909. All events before that date (and possibly for years after, until the municipio of Múgica was formally constituted) were registered under **Apatzingán municipality**.
- Researchers must search Apatzingán's civil registry and Apatzingán's parish (Nuestra Señora de la Asunción) for any birth, baptism, marriage, or death touching this place before ~1909–1915.
- No volume search results returned for "Nueva Italia de Ruiz, Múgica" — zero digitized volumes are specifically filed under that place name on FamilySearch (as of this survey). All digitized records for the area appear under Apatzingán.
- FamilySearch collections_search returned 0 results for Michoacán (no named FamilySearch Historical Records collection is specifically tagged to this state for 1900–1920). Records are accessible via volume_search and the broader Mexico collections.

## Available record types

### Vital records (civil registration)
- **Start date:** Mexico's Registro Civil was established at the national level with the Reform Laws (Leyes de Reforma), beginning ca. 1859–1867. Per the FamilySearch Mexico Vital Records wiki (https://www.familysearch.org/en/wiki/Mexico_Vital_Records): for births *after* 1867, search civil registration first, then Catholic church records.
- **Apatzingán civil birth records (Nacimientos) on FamilySearch — indexed + images:**
  - 1898–1905: digitized and 99–100% name-indexed (searchable via record_search)
  - **1906–1911: NOT PRESENT** in digitized FamilySearch holdings — a significant gap covering Mauro's estimated birth year ~1910. These records may exist in physical archives only.
  - 1912–1921: digitized and 100% name-indexed (searchable), covering years 1912, 1913, 1916–1921
  - **Note: 1914–1915 also absent** from digitized holdings
- **Apatzingán civil death records (Defunciones/Death Records) on FamilySearch — indexed + images:**
  - 1897–1912 present and 100% indexed (year-by-year volumes: 1897, 1898, 1899×2, 1900×3, 1904×4, 1905, 1907, 1908, 1909, 1910, 1911, 1912)
  - 1929, 1930 also indexed
- **Apatzingán civil marriage records (Matrimonios) on FamilySearch — indexed + images:**
  - 1895–1930 well covered, individual-year volumes, nearly all 100% indexed
- **Where held physically:** Registro Civil local office in Apatzingán; Archivo General del Estado de Michoacán (AGEM), Morelia

### Church records
- **Denomination:** Roman Catholic (Archdiocese of Michoacán, est. 1536/1863)
- **Parish:** Nuestra Señora de la Asunción, Apatzingán (principal parish serving the area)
- **Baptism records on FamilySearch:**
  - 1896–1899: indexed (98–100%) and full-text searchable — images exist (image groups 004087244_003, 004087244_004)
  - **1900–1918: NOT PRESENT on FamilySearch** — a major gap. These records likely exist at the Archdiocesan Archive in Morelia or remain in the parish
  - 1919–1920: images exist (volume 004730413_007, Libro 7) covering bautismos, matrimonios, and defunciones; NOT indexed (0% searchable), not full-text searchable — **browse-only**
- **Marriage information (Información matrimonial) from Apatzingán parish:**
  - 1866–1896: browse-only (004730413_004, Libro 4)
  - 1897–1909: browse-only (004730413_005, Libro 5)
  - 1910–1920: browse-only (004730413_006, Libro 6)
  - 1921+: partially indexed
- **Nuestra Señora de Acahuato (neighboring chapel, Apatzingán):** Información matrimonial 1908–1919 — digitized but 0% indexed, not full-text searchable; browse-only (004730412_010, Libro 10)
- **Archdiocese of Morelia marriage information (statewide):** Large indexed collection of *información matrimonial* from the Archdiocese covering 1899–1923 (many volumes, 100% indexed + full-text searchable); these are records from parishes throughout the archdiocese and may include Nueva Italia / Apatzingán
- **Language:** Spanish; Latin for formulaic entries
- **Diocesan archives:** Archivo del Arzobispado de Morelia — holds parish records not yet microfilmed or digitized

### Census records
- **1930 Mexico national census (Censo de población):** FamilySearch holds census volumes for Michoacán municipalities. **Apatzingán** is covered in multiple volumes (004107235_004, 004107235_005, 004107235_006, 004107235_007 — partially indexed 44–76%). No **Múgica** municipality volumes appeared in the first 50 results; it may be covered under Apatzingán or appear on a later page of results (172 total census + government volumes for Michoacán)
- Mexico had no national census between 1910 and 1930 covering individual-household data at this granularity for this region
- **Access:** Some Apatzingán 1930 census volumes are 44–76% indexed; partial name-search possible via record_search

### Probate and court records
- **Ramo Civil (state archive):** Digitized public records from Michoacán 1821–1894 exist on FamilySearch (007984083_002, full-text searchable but 0% name-indexed); any probate or civil court documents would be in this series
- **Where held:** Archivo General del Estado de Michoacán (AGEM) in Morelia; Archivo del Poder Judicial

### Land records
- **Michoacán land and property records:** FamilySearch holds at least one volume (004868365_001) covering Michoacán land records 1870–1906 (100% indexed + full-text searchable)
- **Hacienda records:** Nueva Italia was a hacienda community — company/hacienda labor records, if they survive, would be in private or state archives
- **Where held:** AGEM; Registro Público de la Propiedad in Apatzingán

### Military records
- **Mexican Revolution (1910–1920):** The Tierra Caliente of Michoacán was an active theater. Military conscription and service records for this period are held at the Archivo de la Secretaría de la Defensa Nacional (SEDENA), Mexico City

### Cemetery records
- No FindAGrave or BillionGraves coverage identified for Nueva Italia or Apatzingán for this period. Physical cemetery registers, if extant, would be at the parish or municipal offices.

### Newspaper records
- *El Informador* (Guadalajara, 1917–present) available digitally at http://hemeroteca.informador.com.mx/
- *Hemeroteca Nacional Digital de México* at http://www.hndm.unam.mx/ — national digital newspaper archive

### Immigration / emigration
- **Mexican Border Crossing Records ca. 1903–ca. 1955:** NARA, available at Ancestry (https://www.ancestry.com/search/collections/1082) and via NARA — relevant if Mauro or his relatives migrated to the U.S.
- **Border Crossings From Mexico to U.S., 1895–1964:** Ancestry collection 1082

### Other record types
- **Valladolid Dispensas** (https://www.valladoliddispensas.com/): Marriage dispensations from the Diocesan Archive of Valladolid (now Morelia, Michoacán), pre-1900 primarily; useful for finding family relationships going back one or two generations from Mauro's parents

## Records NOT online
- **Apatzingán civil birth records 1906–1911** — the years most likely covering Mauro Cruz Corona's birth are not present in FamilySearch digitized holdings. These volumes must be requested from the Registro Civil in Apatzingán or AGEM.

## Research Complete — Mauro Cruz Corona's Parentage

**Question answered (q_001, Proved):** *Who were the parents of Mauro Cruz Corona, born about 1910 in or near Nueva Italia, Michoacán, Mexico?*

### Conclusion

**Father: Sostenes Cruz** | **Mother: Ma Apolinar (Apolinar) Corona**

Mauro Cruz Corona's compound surname is itself the fingerprint of this parentage: *Cruz* from his father's family name and *Corona* from his mother's.

### Evidence — Three Independent Sources

| Source | Record | Finding |
|--------|--------|---------|
| **src_001** | Mauro Cruz's church marriage investigation (Información Matrimonial), Parácuaro, Michoacán, 21 Feb 1941 | Groom Mauro Cruz names his own parents: **Sostenes Cruz** (father) and **Ma Apolinar Corona** (mother). Original record; primary information. |
| **src_002** | Primitivo Cruz C's church marriage investigation, Arteaga, Michoacán, 3 Mar 1945 | Mauro's brother Primitivo independently names the **same parents**: Sostenes Cruz and Apolinar Corona. Different document, different informant, different year and town. |
| **src_003** | 1930 Mexico National Census, Nueva Italia de Ruiz, Múgica, Michoacán | **Apolinar Corona** (widowed, born ~1881, Guerrero) lives in the same household as sons Primitivo, **Mauro**, Migel, Libario, and Facundo Cruz — all born in Guerrero. Apolinar's widowed status confirms Sostenes Cruz was deceased before 1930. |

### Key Discovery: Guerrero Origin

The census revealed that **all Cruz family members were born in Guerrero state**, not Michoacán. The family migrated to the Nueva Italia hacienda (Michoacán) at some point before 1930. Any search for Mauro's birth record should be redirected to **Guerrero civil or church records**, not Apatzingán/Michoacán. This opens a natural follow-on question (q_002): Mauro's exact birth date and birthplace within Guerrero.

Score them with the project-relative form, which assembles both documents for you: `same_person({ projectPath, assertionId, treePersonId: "I8" })`. `assertionId` is the assertion the link cites. The tool resolves the record itself and builds the tree side as that person's matching mob, so you hand-build nothing (person-evidence, 'Call it with references, not documents'). If this call was denied, the entire batch was rejected — including any ops in other sections — and must be re-issued after the same_person call. A relationship or marriage assertion names two parties and gets a link for each. The call is about the assertion's own `record_role` party by default; for the OTHER party add `recordRole` (or `recordPersonaId`) naming it. Reusing the first party's persona for the second is how a near-zero score gets manufactured and then explained away. If the tool answers that the record holds no persona for that party, or that the candidate is a stub minted from the very persona you would be scoring (circular), say so in the link's `rationale` and proceed — the gap is still recorded; the rationale is the record of why, not a waiver. How the assertion was RETRIEVED is not such a case: a full-text hit, an image, a PDF and a sidecar-less search are all scorable, because the tool derives the record side from the record's own assertions when it cannot fetch a document. A locally-minted tree id is NOT such a case: it scores on document content and must be scored.
